text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High egress error rate detected in eu-west-2b (AZ-B). Monitoring alert: outbound errors + elevated latency. @oncall paging. https://monitoring.example/alerts/2723456789

sara.ops: saw the pager — several customer APIs failing with timeouts around 04:10Z. 5xx surge from services that call external partners.

lee-net: quick network check: traceroutes from affected instances show return traffic heading to nat-gw in az-c instead of az-b. Looks like route table associations for some subnets changed ~3m ago. Pulling route table state now.

lee-net: dump of relevant routes (sanitized):
```
RouteTable rtb-0123456 (was: az-b-public)
  0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0aaa (nat-azb)
RouteTable rtb-0fedcba (was: az-c-public)
  0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0ccc (nat-azc)
Affected subnets show assoc -> rtb-0fedcba (wrong)
```

tim-deploy: I just applied a terraform change that updated subnet tags to standardize tag:environment values. I did a targeted apply for route associations earlier. Possible I accidentally matched multiple subnets across AZs. 

maria-sre: taking lead. Can we get customer impact estimate? severity?

calvin-support: seeing ~18 open tickets across EU customers all reporting downstream API timeouts and async job failures. No data lost but user-facing errors. Customers affected mostly in eu-west region.

oncall: I'm on rotation but in a 7min window — handing lead to @maria-sre for now. I'll stay available.

maria-sre: mitigation plan (short term):
1) re-associate affected subnets back to the original AZ-specific route table.
2) rebalance NAT gateway attachments to restore SNAT affinity.
3) rollback the tag change in terraform to prevent re-apply drift.
4) monitor error rate and connection success.

lee-net: running re-associate now for two impacted subnets in az-b:
```bash
aws ec2 associate-route-table --subnet-id subnet-0a1b2c3d --route-table-id rtb-0123456
aws ec2 associate-route-table --subnet-id subnet-0b2c3d4e --route-table-id rtb-0123456
```

maria-sre: association calls succeeded for the two subnets. Watching metrics — error rate on the services dropped ~60% in the first 90s. :raised_hands:

tim-deploy: starting rollback of the terraform change (targeting the route table association resource).
```bash
cd infra/vpc
terraform plan -target=module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.tagged_assoc
terraform apply -target=module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.tagged_assoc -auto-approve
```

sara.ops: note — we observed some conntrack / SNAT state imbalance due to mixed egress paths. I manually created a temporary route to prefer nat-azb for affected subnets while connections drain.

lee-net: temporary route snippet applied to fix affinity:
```hcl
resource "aws_route" "force_azb_nat" {
  route_table_id = "rtb-0123456"
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  nat_gateway_id = "nat-0aaa"
}
```

calvin-support: customer reports: recovery seen within ~10 minutes after re-association; majority of tickets auto-updated to resolved by support scripts.

maria-sre: rolling update: rollback complete at 04:16Z. Monitoring shows request error rate back to baseline for affected endpoints. Keeping watch for 30m. Marking as Sev2 for now and will escalate if we see reoccurrence.

oncall: noted handoff — I'm shadowing for the remainder of the window. If anything spikes, ping me directly.

tim-deploy: adding pre-apply validation and tag-uniqueness guard in infra repo. Pushing a quick PR for a precondition check.

lee-net: proposal for guardrail in code to prevent tag collisions (example):
```hcl
locals {
  az_subnets = { for s in var.subnets : s.az => s if length([for t in var.subnets : t if t.az == s.az]) > 0 }
}
# ensure association uses explicit az mapping instead of matching free-form tags
```

maria-sre: timeline so far added to incident doc. We'll run a full postmortem focusing on: human-in-the-loop terraform change, missing pre-apply validation, and runbook gaps around cross-AZ route verification.

sara.ops: quick verification sweep — no cross-AZ SNAT anomalies now, conntrack counts returning to normal.

calvin-support: closing affected customer tickets after confirmation. Reopen if any residuals.

maria-sre: mitigated — moving incident to postmortem. Action items: 1) add terraform precondition, 2) add CI check to reject tag collisions, 3) update oncall runbook to include route-table diff step, 4) schedule postmortem doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> RESOLVED at 04:45Z. Duration: ~00:35:00. Postmortem: https://docs.example/incidents/2723456789

lee-net: big takeaway — never rely on ambiguous tags for critical infrastructure mapping. Will follow up with PR. :memo:

maria-sre: thanks everyone. I'll kick off the postmortem and assign owners for the three action items.

calvin-support: thanks team — customers reporting normal behavior. Closing out. :white_check_mark:
